description: Compliance patterns that must never appear in tracked files of the public tree or in text posted to pull requests. The one pattern file: the scanner in compliance_patterns.py reads it, and the compliance test (platform/tests/tools/test_compliance_patterns.py) runs that scanner over every tracked file. The policy itself lives in platform/AGENTS.md, section Compliance. Changing this file is a privileged change. A pattern that would match its own text writes one letter as a character class (r[a]deon), so this file passes its own scan.

rules.message: link to an internal issue tracker or wiki: write the plain-text issue id instead (for example AICK-1234)
link to an internal document store: describe the content instead of linking it
editor-local link: it points into one developer's session and leaks local state
company host that is not on the public allowlist: remove it, or add the host to 'allowed' in this file if it is publicly reachable
cluster job id: it identifies internal infrastructure; say which device ran the test instead
device bus id: it identifies one internal machine; name the device id (gfx942 and so on) instead
AMD product name: name the gfx target (gfx942, gfx950, ...) instead; where two parts of one target differ, state the hardware fact, for example the CU count
AMD chip codename: name the gfx target (gfx942, gfx950, ...) instead. Codenames that are also ordinary words (Phoenix, Venice, ...) are hits only capitalized after AMD or before a hardware noun
internal site or node name: it identifies internal infrastructure; write a placeholder (<node>, <login-host>) or say what matters about the node (its gfx target, its shared file system) instead
